questions: Have you noticed slowness in activities such as dressing, eating, or turning in bed?
Do you have stiffness or rigidity in your limbs?
Have you noticed a tremor when your hands are resting?
Has your voice become softer or less expressive?
Do you have reduced arm swing when walking?
Does walking improve when you step over a line, follow rhythmic counting, or receive another visual or auditory cue?
Do you freeze especially when turning, approaching a doorway, or rising from a chair?
Have you had falls or near-falls?
Have you developed urinary urgency or incontinence?
Has your memory or thinking noticeably declined?
Has the walking problem progressed more rapidly than your other symptoms?
Did the walking problem begin suddenly?
Have you ever had a stroke or other neurological injury?
Have you taken antipsychotic medicines or medicines for nausea such as metoclopramide or prochlorperazine?
Do you have loss of smell, constipation, or acting out your dreams?
Do you experience visual hallucinations or marked fluctuations in alertness?
Do you have weakness, numbness, dizziness, or loss of balance even when standing still?
